title: Hit v232 on a solo pixel art game project built entirely in a single Claude chat. How do I migrate before context degradation hits me?
author: ArkhamDreamerZero
selftext:
I’m currently a couple of weeks deep into developing a short retro-style pixel art adventure game. I've been doing the whole thing strictly via chat, and I've just hit version 232.

It’s been an incredible ride, but I’m starting to get that creeping sense of dread. The codebase is massive now, and I know how context windows work. I’m terrified of hitting that wall where Claude starts forgetting core architecture, hallucinating old functions, or breaking subtle state logic because it’s losing the thread. Also, the conversation is so huge that it's eating up my Opus tokens insanely fast, maybe there's a workaround too? I'm trying to figure out what my next move should be, and I could use some advice from folks who have pushed long-form software dev further than I have.

Here are my main dilemmas:

# 1. Start Fresh in a New Chat

My first instinct is to export the current code into a fresh chat. But my biggest fear is that Claude will lose all the implicit context (the *why* behind certain design choices, the aesthetic nuances, and the specific quirks of the code's history that got us here).

# 2. Claude Projects?

I haven’t used Claude Projects much, but I'm wondering if this is the exact use case for it. My thought was:

* Export the complete codebase and a detailed design document of the game.
* Spin up a Project.
* Break the work down into separate chats inside that Project - one for core mechanics, one for visuals/rendering, one for sound/music, etc.

Here is my main concern with Projects: If I split them into separate chats, do those chats share the Project's core knowledge base effectively, or do they end up siloed? Since my game systems are deeply interconnected (e.g., visual triggers tied directly to game state and audio managers), I'm worried separate chats won't talk to each other or will give conflicting advice on shared utility scripts.

If you’ve managed long-running game dev workflows or large codebases inside Claude, should I migrate now while it's stable, or ride out the single chat until it breaks? If I move to a Project, what is the best way to structure the files/instructions so I don't lose my momentum or architectural integrity? I don't really have "files" per se, since everything is code in my game, even the music and the SFX.

Would love to hear how others have handled crossing the threshold from "prototyping in a single chat" to "scaling a project." Thanks in a lot!

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body:
Yeah that's the difference between a gamedev and a vibe coder.

A GDD is a document that describes all components of a game. The art style, characters, game mechanics, monetization, world building etc.

Instead of trying to keep the whole game in a chat memory, which is a huge waste of tokens, this document has all the information about your game. You can have multiple chats and multiple agents each look at this document for reference.

replies.author: ArkhamDreamerZero
replies.body: I mean I know what a GDD is, but it's the first time I've heard it used as a programming tool and not as a design bible. But it makes sense now.

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body:
...

It's not a programming tool. It contains all information about the game, design and mechanics. So you can use it for code.

Anyway, keeping the entire project in a single chat is a waste of tokens.

replies.author: ArkhamDreamerZero
replies.body:
"So you can use it for code" - that's what I meant. A tool used for code and not just pre-production pipeline.

But yeah, I'm done with this method. I'm gonna start a Project on Claude with every possible documentation it needs, and then will proceed with smaller individual chats, and keep the Project Knowledge updated.

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Claude Projects already spins off agents/threads for subtasks. Just make sure the main coordinator has access to the GDD (but isn't trying to memorize the whole thing). Another pro tip: tell it to keep a Table of Contents at the top. It'll be very fast to look up info instead of reading the entire doc.

replies.author: ArkhamDreamerZero
replies.body: The Table of Content is a sick idea, thanks. What do you mean by "isn't trying to memorize the whole thing"? Isn't it the point of Project Knowledge? Giving it everything it needs to know so that it's memorized and new chats can be much shorter (and Claude doesn't have to read 2 weeks of prompts).

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body:
It can look up what it needs very fast. No need to memorize the entire document like some kind of exam.

It needs *access* to that information, not the actual information all the time.

How do I explain this. Give it the link to the phone book instead of telling it to memorize the entire phone book just to ask for one number.

comments.author: Figure_431
comments.body:
are you sure Claude never compact the chat? as i know, there is already an option turned on by default "compact when idle" for saving token. 

so you already lost some context. 

Ask Claude to dump the context as MD file into project. you can divide the context by domains like design, code, decision, business logic and etc.

replies.author: ArkhamDreamerZero
replies.body:
It did compact the chat once already.

"Ask Claude to dump the context as MD file into project. you can divide the context by domains like design, code, decision, business logic and etc."

That sounds pretty good. Can I literally ask Claude to do that for me? Like basically figure out the most optimal migration for the game.

replies.author: MarinelordGG
replies.body: Just tell claude to condense everything in a claude.md, then use claude code to use that claude.md and the folder where your project is and to keep documentation, MD files and a short handoff file after every task. Voilaaa, you have a manager to micro manage that will never forget anything

replies.author: Figure_431
replies.body:
i think it did compact every time you walk away longer than 1 hour. 

Yes, Claude can do it for you. Claude actually saves the context as a file somewhere in your disk even thought you didn't ask.

this is how context works

comments.author: r_exel
comments.body: do a small reasearch on llm wiki, i store my gamedesigns in this format and its working well

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body:
Id make the handoff while the old chat is still usable. current working version, architecture, weird decisions and why, known bugs, next task. then actually read it cause the summary can confidently remember things that never happened lol  
save the working code separately too. the handoff is a map, not a replacement for the files

try the new chat on one small bug before trusting it with a big change

replies.author: ArkhamDreamerZero
replies.body: I'll do this monday, cuz right now I've used all my tokens. What exactly should I prompt Claude for it to produce everything I need?

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body:
yeah!  first thing monday in the OLD chat, before adding anything else. try this:

Create a migration handoff for this game's current working version. Mark anything uncertain as unknown rather than guessing. Include setup and run instructions, file structure, systems and dependencies, important decisions and their reasons, known bugs, fixes already attempted, and the next unfinished task. Flag fragile code that should not be casually rewritten. Distinguish features actually implemented from ideas we only discussed.

Provide the current source files, including music and sound effects, and list any assets or dependencies you must save separately. If you cannot recover a complete file, say so instead of silently reconstructing it.

save those files outside the chat and check that the game still runs. then read the handoff for invented details before giving it to the new chat. one small known bug is a good first test good luck
